newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM urges press to shun sensationalism.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM urges press to shun sensationalism.

text.p: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Saturday asked journalists to avoid sensationalism and bias in their reporting and to stick to facts.

"Pen is mighter...but you should use it for objectivity. Confusing people with untrue and motivated writings is not desirable," she told a conference organised by the Dhaka Reporters Unity, a forum of reporters working in local dailies and news agencies.

"My party believes in freedom of press. But journalists have a responsibility to inform people the truth without a bias. And shun sensationalism," said Hasina, in office for three-and-half-months after her Awami League party won general elections in June.
Delegates at the conference demanded an end to "repressive measures" against journalists and free access to information.
They were referring to physical attacks on reporters by rival political activists and police during years of political unrest that forced former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia to resign last March.
"The trend of using government advertisements (to influence newspaper policies) must end. And the Official Secrecy Act should go," said Unity's General Secretary, Mostafa Firoz.
The Act allows officials to hide information or just say "no" to inquiring reporters.
Hasina, however, did not make any immediate promise.
